_meta.indication: Treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in adult patients with narcolepsy

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and modafinil-controlled, 8-week study with a 3-week dose titration phase and a 5-week stable dose phase
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years old with narcolepsy ± cataplexy and ESS ≥14
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) change from baseline at Week 8
pivotal_trials.n: 95 patients randomized (efficacy: WAKIX n=31, placebo n=30)
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean Week-8 ESS 12.4 (WAKIX) vs 15.5 (placebo); placebo-subtracted difference -3.1 (95% CI -5.73, -0.46; p = 0.02)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and modafinil-controlled, 8-week study with a 3-week dose titration phase and a 5-week stable dose phase
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years old with narcolepsy with EDS
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) change from baseline at Week 8
pivotal_trials.n: 166 patients randomized (efficacy: WAKIX n=66, placebo n=32)
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-subtracted ESS difference -2.2 points (95% CI -4.17, -0.22; p = 0.03)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2% and at twice the rate of placebo) were insomnia (6%), nausea (6%), and anxiety (5%); WAKIX also prolongs the QT interval
target_moa: Histamine-3 (H3) receptor inverse agonist/antagonist; binding causes disinhibition of histaminergic neurons and increased synthesis and release of histamine

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug in the intended population

requirement.text: 3675-1: Conduct a prospective, registry-based, observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to pitolisant during pregnancy to an unexposed control population

citations.quote: 3675-1 Conduct a prospective, registry-based, observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to pitolisant during pregnancy to an unexposed control population. The registry will detect and record major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, small for gestational age, preterm birth, and any other adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 3675-2: Conduct a pregnancy study using a different design from the Pregnancy Registry to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, and preterm birth in women exposed to pitolisant during pregnancy

citations.quote: 3675-2 Conduct a pregnancy study that uses a different design from the Pregnancy Registry (e.g., a case control study or a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data with outcome validation) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to pitolisant during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3675-3: Conduct a lactation study in lactating women who received therapeutic doses of pitolisant using a validated assay to assess concentrations of pitolisant in breast milk
